title: China's Battery Consumption Tax Takes Effect — Lithium-Ion Taxed, Solid-State and Sodium-Ion Exempt Through 2028
detail: China ended an 11-year tax exemption for lithium-ion batteries on September 1, 2026, imposing a 2% consumption tax (rising to 4% from September 2027) under rules jointly issued in July by the Ministry of Finance, General Administration of Customs, and State Taxation Administration. Solid-state batteries, sodium-ion batteries, and fuel cells remain exempt through December 31, 2028 — an explicit policy tilt toward next-generation chemistries. The tax takes effect alongside continued pilot-line progress: Sunwoda's dedicated solid-state sample line (0.2 GWh annual design capacity, targeting 400 Wh/kg) reached connectivity in August, and EVE Energy rolled a 60 Ah solid-state prototype off its Longquan line.

title: Return Reaches Financial Close on €400M, 800 MWh Sirius Battery Project in Netherlands
detail: Dutch developer Return reached financial close on September 1, 2026 for its 200 MW/800 MWh (4-hour) Sirius battery storage project in Winschoten, Groningen, backed by a €400 million (~$463 million) financing package from NatWest, Deutsche Bank, ABN AMRO, Rabobank, and NG. The close was underpinned by a new long-term fixed-price toll agreement with utility Vattenfall — Return and Vattenfall's second such deal after the 100 MW/200 MWh Antares project in Waddinxveen (April 2025), and one of the largest fixed-price BESS tolls signed in the Netherlands to date. The project connects to grid operator TenneT under a time-dependent transport-rights arrangement and targets commercial operations in Q4 2027.
